displayCalibration.noChanges: No changes yet. Record a reference, adjust the device, then refresh current values.

displayCalibration.exportNotes: Generated by ADB Manager Display Color; visibleEffectConfirmed=false means the screen still needs physical validation.
displayCalibration.vendorHelperRequired: This item comes from the device Settings vendor display API. ADB Manager routes it through the helper; production firmware may still deny shell-to-display-HAL access.

Root can trigger device reconnects or reboots; a successful readback proves the property value, while live screen refresh depends on firmware applying it immediately.

agent.title: Agent Tasks
agent.newEvidenceDraftBlocked: Stop the current {{kind}} before starting a new record.
promptSuggestions: Give me a device report with Android version, storage, memory, battery, and key package status.
Why is Launcher laggy? Collect CPU, memory, frame timing, thermal, and foreground process evidence.
The current page is black. Check whether this points to Launcher, SystemUI, SurfaceFlinger, or display pipeline failure.
Google Calendar is not syncing. Check accounts, sync adapters, network, and JobScheduler state.
APK install failed. Check system restrictions, package conflicts, signature/version state, and storage headroom.
Wireless ADB will not connect. Check device-side wireless debugging, network address, and adbd state.
Touch is not responding. Check input devices, focused window, and InputDispatcher evidence.
An app icon disappeared. Check whether the package is disabled, Launcher visibility, and default handlers.
Network is unavailable. Check Wi-Fi, routes, DNS, and Connectivity state.
The app crashed or ANR happened. Collect recent fatal, ANR, tombstone, and dropbox clues.
Storage looks abnormal. Check /data usage, cache pressure, and low-storage logs.
Generate a device diagnosis report that I can send to engineering.
Home performance regressed. Compare CPU, GPU, memory, frame rate, and thermal evidence.
Check the current foreground app, Activity, window focus, and page hierarchy.
Check accessibility issues: button descriptions, tap target size, and visible text.
Run a 10-minute stress check and watch for crashes, ANRs, and key logs.
Analyze why startup is slow using logcat, process launch, IO, and main-thread clues.
Check whether the device recently rebooted, system services failed, or key processes died.
Check whether the Agent APK is installed, started, and reporting sampling data.
Compare key package versions, permissions, performance, and storage before and after upgrade.

pairConnect.lanDevicesDesc: Android wireless debugging devices discovered via mDNS
pairConnect.firstTimeHint: If this is the first time connecting this device, please enable pairing code in Android wireless debugging and complete pairing first.
pairConnect.autoConnectNone: Auto-connect attempted, no online devices found
pairConnect.connectPortPlaceholder: Port shown on wireless debugging page
pairConnect.howToGetPairCode: How to get the pairing code
pairConnect.guideStep1: On your Android device, open Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging
pairConnect.guideStep3: Tap Pair device with pairing code
pairConnect.guideStep4: The screen will display a 6-digit pairing code and pairing port number — enter them in the pairing section above
pairConnect.howToGetConnectAddr: How to get the connection IP and port
pairConnect.guideConnectStep1: On your Android device, open Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging
pairConnect.guideConnectStep2: The IP address and port displayed on the page is the connection address (note: this port differs from the pairing port)
pairConnect.guideConnectStep3: Enter the IP and port in the connection section above
pairConnect.guideTip: Tip: Pairing is only needed once — subsequent connections don't require re-pairing. LAN scanning will automatically discover devices and fill in the addresses. If a device can't be found, make sure wireless debugging is enabled in Android developer options, and try switching Wi-Fi and rescanning.
pairConnect.noDeviceHintTitle: If no devices are found, use manual connection
pairConnect.noDeviceHintDesc: Check the IP address and port on Android's wireless debugging page, and enter them in the "Connect Device" section below. This port changes — don't use old ports or the pairing port from the pairing code dialog.
pairConnect.recentConnectionsDesc: When scanning finds nothing, check recently connected addresses first. If the port is still reachable, reconnect directly.
pairConnect.tryRestartReconnect: If the port is reachable but still fails, try "Restart ADB and reconnect".
pairConnect.repairWirelessPairingDesc: Safe repair refreshes the wireless pairing cache while preserving this computer's ADB identity.
pairConnect.repairNoDevice: {{message}}, but no devices were found. Check the current IP and port shown on Android's wireless debugging page, then try manual connection.
pairConnect.resetHostIdentityDesc: Use only after restarting ADB still fails. This computer will need to be re-authorized or paired again on all Android devices.
pairConnect.resetConfirmDesc: This removes adb_known_hosts.pb, adbkey, and adbkey.pub. All authorized or paired Android devices may need to authorize or pair this computer again. Try safe repair first.

recovery.title: Wireless recovery ladder
recovery.desc: Work down the ladder: check network and discovery first, then recent endpoints and the current Android port. Safe repair comes before host identity reset.
recovery.multiNetwork: Multiple local networks detected. Confirm the computer and Android device are on the same Wi-Fi/subnet.

network.title: Network and ADB state

repair.title: Safe wireless repair

performance.title: Performance Sampling
performance.sampleTimeout: ADB sampling timed out: no response within 20 seconds, so auto sampling was paused. Confirm the device is still online or try Start/Sample now again.
performance.streamFallback: Persistent sampling stream is unavailable. Fell back to compatibility sampling: {{reason}}
performance.agentConnected: Agent connected; system-level metrics are still supplemented by ADB.
performance.agentPermissionLimited: Agent connected with limited Android permissions; ADB supplement remains active.
performance.agentUpdateAvailable: Agent update available. Enabling Agent installs the bundled APK with app data preserved.
performance.agentEnableFailed: Agent enable failed: {{reason}}. ADB-only sampling remains active.
performance.agentSampleFallback: Agent sample is unavailable. Fell back to ADB-only: {{reason}}
performance.agentStopped: Agent stopped. ADB-only sampling remains active.
performance.pinHelpFollowing: By default this follows the foreground app. Pin the target app after opening it so the target does not change when you switch to Settings or Home.
performance.pinHelpPinned: This package stays as the sampling target even when another screen moves to the foreground.
performance.noPackageToPin: No foreground package to pin yet
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryUsageAvailable: GPU usage counters are readable; the trend chart will update with samples.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryCountersPermissionLi: The device blocks adb shell from reading GPU usage or frequency counters; memory and frame stats may still be available.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryMemoryAndFrequencyOn: Only GPU memory and frequency are readable; no busy/load counter is available for usage calculation.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryMemoryOnly: Only GPU memory is readable, usually from dumpsys gpu; it does not represent GPU usage.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryFrequencyOnly: Only GPU frequency is readable; no busy/load counter is available for usage calculation.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryMetadataOnly: The device returned some raw GPU info, but no displayable usage, frequency, or memory value.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryUnavailable: This device does not expose readable GPU counters, usually because of system permissions or vendor node limits.
performance.gpuDiagnosticSummaryNotSampled: GPU probe results will appear after the first performance sample.
performance.alertProcessGone: The target process exited or is not visible.
performance.alertMemory: RSS grew by more than 20% in the last 5 minutes.

apkInstall.title: Install APK
apkInstall.dropHint: Drag APKs or folders containing APKs here, or click Select Files
apkInstall.pasteHint: You can also copy APKs or folders in Finder, then return here and press Cmd/Ctrl+V or click Paste.
apkInstall.searchHint: Typing searches automatically; click a suggested package to select it
apkInstall.forceInstallDesc: Force install will uninstall the existing package first, then install the current APK
apkInstall.parseFailed: Could not auto-detect package name — please enter it manually for force install
apkInstall.parseFailedNonForce: Could not auto-detect package name; normal install can still continue
apkInstall.forceNeedPkg: Force install requires a package name
apkInstall.forceNeedPkgMultiple: Force install requires a package name for every APK
apkInstall.forceMultiDesc: Multi-APK force install uninstalls each detected package before installing that APK
apkInstall.noDevice: Select an online device before installing
apkInstall.note1: Default mode is overlay install (preserves data). Check "Force install" to clear data.
apkInstall.note2: Force install uninstalls the old version first (data will be lost), then installs the new version
apkInstall.note3: Installation may require confirming install permissions on the device
apkInstall.note4: Multiple APKs are installed sequentially; failures are recorded and the next APK continues
